text: dsh-git-graph-sidebar 是面向 DSH Web 的 Git 管理插件，提供工作区仓库图谱侧栏和会话输入区分支芯片。它通过主机 Git 服务及浏览器界面呈现提交图、分支状态和关联工作树，并提供提交规范文档引导与规则提示。用户可查看多仓库、切换或新建分支、复制提交信息、初始化仓库，以及由 git_worktree 工具管理工作树。适合在 DSH 中浏览项目历史和保持团队提交约定的开发者；图谱侧栏需要 dsh-better-sidebar。

dsh-git-graph-sidebar adds a Git graph sidebar and branch chip to DSH. It displays repository history, branches and worktrees, supports branch changes and commit detail copying, and provides commit convention guidance. The git_worktree tool manages worktrees; the sidebar requires dsh-better-sidebar.
想在 DSH 里直接查看项目的 Git 提交图和分支状态。
有没有办法在一个工作区里浏览多个嵌套仓库的历史？
我想从对话输入区快速切换或新建当前项目分支。
怎样在 DSH 里查看提交详情并把信息复制给助手？
I want to inspect a project’s commit graph and branch state inside DSH.
Can I manage Git worktrees and open them as DSH workspaces?
I need a sidebar that discovers nested repositories in my workspace.
Help me keep commit messages aligned with repository conventions.
dsh-git-graph-sidebar 的功能「仓库图谱」：在侧栏发现工作区中的 Git 仓库并展示提交关系、分支引用和状态，支持查看提交详情、缩放图谱及复制提交信息。
dsh-git-graph-sidebar 的功能「分支芯片」：在空白会话的输入区显示当前仓库分支入口，可查看分支并切换或创建分支；也可打开提交图和工作树管理界面。
dsh-git-graph-sidebar 的功能「工作树管理」：助手调用 git_worktree 工具可初始化仓库或创建、列出、移除受管理的 Git worktree；新工作树会登记为 DSH workspace。
dsh-git-graph-sidebar 的功能「提交规范」：为仓库建立提交约定文档，并把可识别的规则提供给助手；可使用内置框架或自定义模板，严格模式还能安装提交消息检查钩子。
dsh-git-graph-sidebar 每日最多向 dsh-market.com 发送安装心跳，含插件名、版本和随机浏览器标识；遥测退出设置或 DNT 可停止发送。（src/client/telemetry.ts:117-147）

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · dsh-git-graph-sidebar：A Git plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): a branch chip in the composer, a **Repository graph** tab inside [dsh-better-sidebar](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-better-sidebar), and — opt-in — the same graph as a page in the conversation's main area. It lists the Git repositories found up to three levels below the workspace, draws the selected repository's commit graph as an SVG lane canvas, and turns that repository's commit conventions into something both you and the model actually follow.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Why this one：Plenty of plugins draw a commit graph. This one is built around the part that decides whether a commit message comes out right, and the three guarantees below are not on offer elsewhere:

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Why this one：1. **The rules reach the model, not just the panel.** The convention document is registered as a `systemPrompt` section, so every model step is told what this repository wants before it writes anything, instead of learning it from a rejection. `strict: true` goes further: the block tells the assistant to rewrite an offending message before committing.
2. **The rules are read back, prose included.** Machine-checkable rules (type prefixes, subject length, case, trailing period, mood, subject language) are parsed out of the document — and out of an `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` sitting beside it — so a repository that never wrote a `GIT_CONVENTIONS.md` is still understood. A backward-compatible `ai: required | optional | forbidden` field then checks the trailers in commit **bodies**, which is where attribution actually lives.
3. **Two documents that disagree never get silently outvoted.** Dropping a plugin into a running project is the usual way a second convention document appears. The tab compares the workspace document, the repository document and a parent repository's document field by field and rule by ru

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Why this one：Everything runs locally against the loopback endpoint the host already provides: no network calls, no telemetry, and every Git command is a read except the switches you press yourself.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Repository graph tab (better-sidebar)：The tab works from the session's working directory and treats that directory as a container: Git repositories up to three levels below it are reachable without registering each repository as a separate DSH workspace.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Repository graph tab (better-sidebar)：- **Multi-repository discovery** — the workspace root itself, plus repositories nested up to 3 levels below it. Each entry carries its current branch, short head, dirty-file count and conflict count.
- **A scan that costs what it should** — one `git for-each-ref` per repository returns the branch time, the upstream and the ahead/behind distance in one call; while the refs have not moved the whole answer comes from the last scan, and only the status probe (dirty files, conflicts) is repeated. A workspace full of repositories no longer gets slower with every extra one.
- **Repository tree** — the root, the intermediate directories and each repository, so the level relationship between them is visible rather than implied by a path.
- **Linked checkouts, read-only** — a repository row expands to its linked worktrees (`git worktree list`), each with its branch and HEAD. Picking one switches the status strip to that checkout's branch, HEAD and dirty state and marks its HEAD row on the graph — one graph, not one per checkout: linked worktrees share refs and objects, so the commit list is the same everywhere. From there t

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Repository graph tab (better-sidebar)：- **The rules in force, at a glance** — the conventions strip lists the checkable rules the document itself states as small chips: `type: feat / fix / docs`, `subject ≤ 72`, `lowercase start`, `no trailing period`, `imperative`, plus `Chinese` / `English` / `Chinese + English` when the document names a subject language, and an amber *Strict* chip for a strict document. What you see is exactly what the agent is told. It does **not** tally commits that are already written: nothing in the panel can change them, so a count would be noise. A document with no checkable rule says so instead of guessing.
- **Upgrade preview** — on a repository that already carries a document, *Switch framework* no longer overwrites it: the tab first shows *What would change* — how many sections are added, rewritten or removed, with the titles — and nothing is written until *Write it* is pressed. *Cancel* leaves the file untouched.
- **Workspace document** — once the workspace holds more than one repository a *Workspace conventions* strip appears under the toolbar and writes `<workspace>/.dsh/GIT_CONVENTIONS.md` in one click; a repository

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Branch chip (composer)：The chip that ships with the upstream plugin is unchanged: on a blank conversation it lets you switch or create a branch, and it opens the interactive commit-graph dialog and the worktree manager. Branch operations run in the host process; the chip hides itself on active sessions.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Requirements：| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| Node (host runtime) | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |
| `dsh-better-sidebar` | needed **for the tab only** — without it the plugin still loads and the chip keeps working |

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Install：Grab the prebuilt bundle from the [latest release](https://github.com/Athosoo/dsh-git-graph-sidebar/releases/latest) — `dsh-git-graph-sidebar.tgz`, no build step needed — then install it as a plugin bundle:

- **Desktop app (the `desktop` profile is owned by the Electron app, so the CLI refuses it):** install the `.tgz` from the app's plugin page.
- **CLI-managed profile:**

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Install：```sh
  dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Athosoo/dsh-git-graph-sidebar
  # or from the downloaded tarball
  dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-git-graph-sidebar.tgz
  ```

**Restart DSH after installing.** The host half registers its `/git/*` HTTP routes at startup, so a page refresh alone is not enough for a first install, and an upgraded build is not picked up until the process restarts.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Install：The tab needs [`dsh-better-sidebar`](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) installed; without it everything else — the branch chip, the graph dialog, worktrees — keeps working and only the sidebar tab is absent.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Repository discovery rules：| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scan depth | 3 levels below the working directory (a repository found at a level is not descended into) |
| Upper bound | 200 repositories per scan, then the result is flagged as truncated |
| Skipped directory names | `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `out`, `coverage`, `target`, `vendor` — plus every dot-directory |
| Repository marker | a `.git` entry (directory, file or symlink — so worktrees and submodules are both detected) |
| Per-entry status budget | 5 s; an entry whose `git status` did not return in time is still listed, without branch metadata |
| Cache | 60 s per base path, shared between concurrent requests; the tab's refresh button bypasses it |

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Git conventions：A commit graph shows what happened; a conventions document records what the team agreed to do next time. The tab can bootstrap that document for every repository it lists.

- **Bring your own document** — the plugin never invents house rules. It writes an empty scaffold with six sections marked `待定` / *to decide* and `status: draft`, so the team fills in the decisions instead of inheriting someone else's defaults.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Git conventions：- **Triggered by a new repository** — a repository that has no document and no commits yet (`unborn HEAD`) gets the empty scaffold automatically, and the framework picker opens right away. Repositories that already contain commits but no document are listed as missing it; one click writes the scaffold.

- **Seven proven frameworks** — picking one writes its full template into the document and flips it to `status: settled`:

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Git conventions：| Framework | Best for |
  | --- | --- |
  | Conventional Commits | changelogs and semantic versions generated from commit messages |
  | GitHub Flow | small teams shipping from `main` with short-lived feature branches |
  | Git Flow | versioned releases promoted across several environments |
  | Trunk-based development | continuous delivery with very short-lived branches |
  | Conventional Branch | branch names that encode type and issue reference |
  | GitLab Flow | explicit environment branches between `main` and production |
  | Worktree flow | several versions or hotfixes checked out at once |

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Git conventions：- **Never overwrites** — an existing document is only replaced when the request carries `force`, which the UI does not offer for settled documents. The document is plain Markdown in the repository root, so it is reviewed and revised like any other source file.
- **My templates** — the gear at the right end of the toolbar opens a one-entry *Settings* menu, and *Template management* takes you to the manager (the picker's *Manage templates* button jumps straight there): write the team's own rules as a template (id, name, tagline, best-for, reference URL, body), and it appears in a *My templates* group at the end of the framework picker with a *Custom* badge; the seven built-in frameworks stay read-only and cannot be edited or deleted; the same page lists them above your templates with a show/hide switch, which only removes their card from the picker (`POST /git/convention/templates` action `toggle`, stored as `hiddenBuiltins`) and never touches a body, so a document already carrying that framework keeps resolving. Saving forces `framework: <template id>` and a `status:` line into the front matter, rejects a body over 64 KB or without `sta

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Initializing a repository：A workspace does not have to start as a repository. When the root of the workspace is not one, the tab's toolbar offers **Initialize Git repository** (and a workspace with no repositories at all shows the same button in the empty panel).

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Initializing a repository：- **Two steps, never one click** — the button opens a bar that names the target directory and the initial branch before anything is written.
- **Only `.git` is written** — `git init` creates the metadata directory; no file in the workspace is touched, and existing repositories below the workspace are unaffected.
- **It refuses to nest** — if the directory already sits inside a repository (including a parent outside the workspace), the host answers `already-repository` instead of creating a second root inside it.
- **It hands over to the conventions flow** — because the new repository has no commits yet, the empty conventions document is scaffolded and the framework picker opens immediately, so the first commit already follows an agreed rule set.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · HTTP routes：Registered by the host half under `/git`; all of them answer JSON (`{ok:true,value}` / `{ok:false,error}`), except `/git/events`, which is a server-sent event stream.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · HTTP routes：| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/git/repos` | multi-repository discovery for a path (`{path, refresh?}`) |
| `/git/status` | branch, head, dirty/untracked/conflict counts |
| `/git/branches` | branch list with the current one marked |
| `/git/graph` | commit list with parents and refs (`{path, limit?}`) |
| `/git/switch` | switch branch |
| `/git/create-branch` | create and switch |
| `/git/worktrees` | worktree list |
| `/git/worktree-add` | create a worktree |
| `/git/worktree-remove` | remove a worktree |
| `/git/worktree/list` | linked worktrees of a repository, read-only (`{path}`; the anchor must sit inside a registered workspace, the answer is `git worktree list --porcelain` with `bare`/`locked`/`prunable`/`detached` kept) |
| `/git/worktree/status` | branch, HEAD and dirty state read in one linked checkout (`{path, worktree}`; `worktree` is matched against the list, never used as a cwd directly) |
| `/git/worktree/branches` | branch list of one linked checkout (`{path, worktree}`) |
| `/git/worktree/graph` | commit list read in one linked checkout (`{path, worktree, limit?}`) |
| `/git/conventions` | convention document state

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · HTTP routes：| `/git/events` | change notifications (polled by the UI) |

Every route resolves the requested path with `realpath` and rejects it unless it lands inside a registered workspace. Nested repository directories are accepted; anything outside a workspace gets `workspace-unknown`.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Known limitations：- **The tab never changes an existing repository's Git state.** It writes the conventions document, and it can run `git init` for a directory that is not a repository yet — nothing else. No commits, no branch switching, no worktree creation or removal: those stay in the chip's dialog. Linked checkouts are listed read-only, and a jump only opens a session or a workspace — it never creates a worktree.
- **Linked checkouts outside every registered workspace are listed but not readable.** The four `/git/worktree/*` routes gate the *repository* the checkout belongs to, so a checkout that is not registered as a workspace itself still gets its branch, HEAD and dirty state; the jump then registers it on request.
- **Do not install this alongside `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph`.** Both halves own the `/git` route prefix, and two registrations of the same prefix conflict. Install one or the other.
- **Repositories deeper than 3 levels are not listed**, and a repository inside a skipped directory name (`node_modules`, `dist`, …) is not listed either, by design.
- **The host half is a build output.** `lib/index.js` is edited directly (the a

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Development：```sh
npm run build     # splice src/client/graph/SidebarTab.js into lib/client.js
npm run check     # node --check on both bundles
npm run validate  # every t("…") key exists in both locale dictionaries
npm run preview   # render the tab to preview/*.html without a running DSH

`npm run preview` writes standalone HTML files (dark and light theme) that show the tab with sample repositories and commits, so layout changes can be checked in a browser without installing anything.

dsh-git-graph-sidebar README · Attribution and license：This is a fork of [`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-git-graph) 0.4.8 by linxin666, also Apache-2.0. The branch chip, the commit-graph dialog, the worktree manager and the host git service come from that project. Changes in this fork: renamed package, workspace gate widened from exact-path match to inside-a-workspace, added the `/git/repos` discovery route, added the better-sidebar tab (repository tree, SVG canvas, zoom, pinned commit card) and its locale keys, and since 1.15.0 the tab lists linked checkouts read-only through four `/git/worktree/*` routes and can jump to one.
